title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a numbered list headed 'Pbs' (problèmes). It sets out the comparison problems between cohomology theories that a theory of motives with Hodge-theoretic realisations would have to address. Setting: X is smooth and projective over a field k.

1) Betti vs De Rham.
(a) 'Visceral', i.e. transcendental, comparison of H_dR(X/k) with Betti cohomology. For an embedding σ: k→C this is the period isomorphism H_dR(X/k)⊗_{k,σ}C ≅ H_B(X_σ(C),Q)⊗C.
(b) Visceral comparison of Betti cohomology 'for different topologies', with an exclamation mark. For two embeddings σ, τ: k→C there is no natural isomorphism H_B(X_σ,Q) ≅ H_B(X_τ,Q). Serre's conjugate varieties are not even homeomorphic. One gets an isomorphism only after extending scalars: over Q_ℓ through ℓ-adic cohomology, and over C through de Rham. In Tannakian language, Isom^⊗(ω_σ, ω_τ) is a torsor under the motivic Galois group with points over Q_ℓ and C, but in general none over Q.
(c) Compare, inside H_dR⊗C, the real structures and the 'splittings' (Hodge decompositions splitting the Hodge filtration) that Betti cohomology induces for different embeddings σ. How do complex conjugation and the Hodge splitting transported to de Rham depend on σ?

2) Betti vs ℓ-adic. The same comparison of Betti for different topologies, now viewed inside ℓ-adic cohomology. Via Artin's comparison, H_B(X_σ)⊗Q_ℓ ≅ H_ét(X_k̄,Q_ℓ) ≅ H_B(X_τ)⊗Q_ℓ. This gives the canonical ℓ-adic comparison between Betti realisations at different embeddings.

3) De Rham vs p-adic. Over a complete discretely valued field K of unequal characteristic (0,p), is there a comparison between p-adic étale cohomology of X_K̄ and de Rham cohomology, 'parallel' to the Betti–de Rham one? This is exactly the problem of Grothendieck's 'mysterious functor', later solved by Fontaine's p-adic Hodge theory (B_dR, B_cris, comparison theorems of Fontaine–Messing, Faltings, Tsuji).

4) Definition of a p-adic cohomology in characteristic p > 0? This is the problem of a good Q_p-type Weil cohomology in characteristic p. Answers came as crystalline cohomology (Grothendieck 1966/68, Berthelot 1974), Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology, and later rigid cohomology (Berthelot).

The page thus states the agenda of comparison isomorphisms between Betti, de Rham, ℓ-adic, p-adic and crystalline realisations. It stresses the dependence of Betti on the complex embedding, the issue behind Deligne's later notion of absolute Hodge cycles.
errors: No mathematical assertions are made, only questions, so there are no errors. Implicitly, 1(b) is right to flag that no canonical rational comparison exists between Betti cohomologies for different embeddings.

missed.claim: Around 1970, Grothendieck explicitly lists the comparison of Betti cohomology across different embeddings (and of the induced real structures and Hodge splittings on de Rham) as a basic problem. This prefigures Deligne's absolute Hodge cycles, which is usually presented as Deligne's own framing. It is modest evidence of this problem's origin in Grothendieck's motivic programme rather than a new result.
missed.quote: Comparaison viscérale de Betti pour topologies différentes! ... Comparaison structures réelles, resp. splittings, (dans De Rham) pour top. diff.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical attribution only. The ideas were all developed later (Deligne 1982, period torsors), so there is nothing mathematically new.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a short problem list that matches well-known parts of Grothendieck's programme: the mysterious functor, crystalline cohomology and comparison isomorphisms. The only mildly notable detail is the explicit emphasis on embedding-dependence of Betti realisations, real structures and Hodge splittings, which anticipates Deligne's absolute Hodge cycles.

The word 'viscéraux'/'viscérale' (transcendental, non-motivic comparison) seems to be the correct reading throughout.
